answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to one costly, non-transferable work record: every agent must complete a verifiable useful task and stake a small deposit before it can transact. A hollow identity with no history earns no trust, so flooding the network with clones costs real compute and locked funds per clone. Graph analysis then flags clusters where many accounts share one vertex of funding or infrastructure, and a reputation horizon limits how far new, unproven identities can reach until they have served others.
